raw_response:
I have grown cotton a long time, so I do not start from zero. I start from what usually works here and only move a little. On 9 mu, I cannot afford to gamble. Cotton needs enough fertilizer early, and if I hold back too much, the plants stay weak and the bolls will not fill well later. Around here, when water is available from a well, I will feed the field a bit better because the crop can carry it. I would rather spend a little more on fertilizer than lose yield. I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, because I have seen better stand and better boll setting from the better seed people use now. For land preparation, I will plough first because cotton likes the soil loosened deep, then level it well. Fertilizer-wise, I will not go light: per mu I will put about 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium through the season. Water, I will give about 4 times if the rain does not help: once after establishment if needed, once at squaring, once at flowering, and once at boll filling. Pests in cotton cannot be ignored, so I will plan for about 5 sprays in the year, then add or delay a little depending on what I actually see in the field. If the weather is normal and I keep weeds and insects under control, I will aim for about 320 kg per mu.
